topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the learning objectives for understanding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional Treatments: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review traditional cancer treatment modalities that non-specifically eliminate tumor tissue and rapidly dividing cells, discussing their therapeutic limits and mechanisms of toxicity and resistance.

topics.label: Targeting Intrinsic Vulnerabilities: Hormone Dependence, Checkpoints, and DNA Repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how therapeutic strategies can selectively exploit inherent weaknesses in cancer cells, including hormone signaling requirements, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethal DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction and Kinase Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the identification of driver oncogenes, the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting ATP binding pockets, and the clinical challenges of target mutation and bypass resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover antibody-based approaches that direct cytotoxicity against cancer cells by targeting surface antigens or delivering conjugated toxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the role of the immune system in tumor surveillance and examine methods to activate anti-tumor immune responses through checkpoint blockade, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Current Challenges, Future Directions, and Clinical Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the broader clinical realities of cancer management, focusing on tumor heterogeneity, evolving diagnostic tools, long-term survival trends, and ethical considerations in treatment selection.
